b.request: Count execution records per order type, filter for types whose share strictly exceeds the mean share, and return their total count, mean share, and mean excess above the overall mean.
b.sql: WITH exec_counts AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) as exec_count FROM orderexecutions oe JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), total_execs AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_count FROM exec_counts), shares AS (SELECT ec.ordertune, ec.exec_count, CAST(ec.exec_count AS FLOAT) / te.total_count as share FROM exec_counts ec CROSS JOIN total_execs te), mean_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) as mean_share_val FROM shares), filtered_shares AS (SELECT s.ordertune, s.exec_count, s.share, ms.mean_share_val, s.share - ms.mean_share_val as excess FROM shares s CROSS JOIN mean_share ms WHERE s.share > ms.mean_share_val) SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_count, AVG(share) as mean_share, AVG(excess) as mean_excess FROM filtered_shares

c.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and ignore executions without a matching order. Find how many executed orders each order type (`ordertune`) has, with a missing order type treated as its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share. Count execution records per order type, so each fill counts separately, and then compute shares and the above-average summary from those counts.
c.sql: WITH exec_by_type AS (SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(*) as exec_count FROM orderexecutions oe INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.ordertune), total_stats AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total_count FROM exec_by_type), shares AS (SELECT ebt.ordertune, ebt.exec_count, ebt.exec_count::FLOAT / ts.total_count as share FROM exec_by_type ebt CROSS JOIN total_stats ts), avg_share_val AS (SELECT AVG(share) as avg_share FROM shares), filtered AS (SELECT s.ordertune, s.exec_count, s.share, asv.avg_share FROM shares s CROSS JOIN avg_share_val asv WHERE s.share > asv.avg_share) SELECT SUM(exec_count) as sum_counts, AVG(share) as avg_share_above_average, AVG(share - avg_share) as avg_excess FROM filtered

d.request: Count execution records per order type by joining orderexecutions to orders on recordvault=ordersmark (excluding unmatched executions, treating NULL ordertune as a distinct group), calculate each type's share as execution_count/total_executions, filter to types with share strictly exceeding the mean share across all types, and return the sum of execution counts for above-average types, their arithmetic mean share, and their arithmetic mean excess (share minus overall average share).
d.sql:
WITH execution_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(oe.orderexecmark) as exec_count
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = oe.ordersmark
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
total_executions AS (
  SELECT COUNT(oe.orderexecmark) as total_exec
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  JOIN orders o ON o.recordvault = oe.ordersmark
),
execution_shares AS (
  SELECT ec.ordertune, ec.exec_count, 1.0 * ec.exec_count / te.total_exec as share
  FROM execution_counts ec
  CROSS JOIN total_executions te
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as mean_share
  FROM execution_shares
),
above_average AS (
  SELECT es.exec_count, es.share, av.mean_share
  FROM execution_shares es
  CROSS JOIN avg_share av
  WHERE es.share > av.mean_share
)
SELECT SUM(exec_count) as sum_executions, AVG(share) as mean_share, AVG(share - mean_share) as mean_excess
FROM above_average;

a.request: Link each order execution to its order (where `recordvault` matches `ordersmark`), and drop any execution without a matching order. Count execution records per order type (`ordertune`); an order with several executions counts once per execution, and a missing order type forms its own group. Then work out each type's share of the total count as a fraction. Looking only at the order types whose share is strictly above the average share across all order types, return a single unrounded row with: the sum of their counts, their average share, and the average amount by which their share exceeds that overall average share.
a.sql:
WITH type_counts AS (
  SELECT o.ordertune, COUNT(oe.orderexecmark) as exec_count
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  INNER JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  GROUP BY o.ordertune
),
total_count AS (
  SELECT SUM(exec_count) as total FROM type_counts
),
shares AS (
  SELECT 
    tc.ordertune,
    tc.exec_count,
    CAST(tc.exec_count AS FLOAT) / (SELECT total FROM total_count) as share
  FROM type_counts tc
),
avg_all AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) as avg_val FROM shares
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT ordertune, exec_count, share
  FROM shares
  WHERE share > (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_all)
)
SELECT 
  SUM(exec_count) as sum_counts,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(share) - (SELECT avg_val FROM avg_all) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg
